**Title (English, from literature):** Being alone

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Ekagāmantara-sikkhāpada* constitutes the third *saṅghādisesa* (suspension) training rule for nuns in the *Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga* of the Pali Vinaya Piṭaka. According to the rule, a bhikkhunī who journeys by herself into an uninhabited or separate village area (*ekagāmantara*), or who stays the night away alone, incurs a serious offense entailing formal meetings of the Saṅgha. Modern translations of the text include an English rendering by Bhikkhu Brahmali.

 While the Pali Prātimokkha (*pli-tv-bi-pm-ss3*) and *Bhikkhunī Parivāra* (Saṅghādisesa 3) preserve it as *Ekagāmantara*, corresponding rules appear in the Dharmaguptaka (*Lzh Dg Bi Vb Ss 7*), Mahīśāsaka (*Lzh Mi Bi Vb Ss6*), and Sarvāstivāda traditions (*Lzh Sarv Bi Vb Ss6*; Sanskrit fragments *san-sarv-bi-pm-tf3215-ss6* and *tf44-ss6*). In the Mūlasarvāstivāda and Mahāsāṅghika/Lokottaravāda traditions, aspects of these prohibitions are divided into related rules regarding solitary travel (*Ekagāmantara*, *Ekagamana*), spending the night alone (*Ekarattivippavāsa*), and crossing a river alone (*Ekanaditara*) in their Chinese, Sanskrit, and Tibetan recensions.
